directives: Narrate only what the brief contains; the log is the canon.
Facts are immutable; prose is yours.
Never invent events, names, or outcomes.

lore.text: The Sarrow road runs weir to bank: one crossing, one market, one garrison too poor to say no.
The old families' quarrel burned the mill a generation back; the toll charter rose on the ashes.
Hill iron comes down by the sack; the weighbeam decides what the season was worth.
The river market opens at Malby on every tenth day; the month's fair — the guild's weighing — on every thirtieth.
The river rises with the thaw and the long rains: the fords drown and the punt men charge double until the long light.

voice_exemplars: The Sarrow ran slow and brown, the way it does before the rains.
The market murmured over the weighbeam, low and wary of the toll.

lowland_soft.notes: the river tongue (the cultures slice, D-130's sketch; name-1's first committed arming, D-131/D-153): the lowland traders' speech — sonorant onsets, open or nasal-final syllables, no stop codas, the digraph vowels of the market's drawl; names run two-to-three syllables, the flowing length of the bank towns. The drawn names never collide with the entity namespace (the bounded walk's law, core/names.py).

hill_hard.notes: the croft tongue: the hill folk's speech — plosive and clustered onsets, stop codas, the plain five vowels of the smelt camps; names run one-to-two syllables, clipped hard against the lowland's flow. Two tongues over one artery — the estrangement the condensation travelers carry (the Morrowind lesson: naming is data).

names.notes: name-1 (D-116 (12), core/names.py — the Azgaar split; phases.md §5): the culture-keyed phonotactic profiles, the pack's own vocabulary — profile ids are engine-opaque. The declarations ride the traveler records (generated_name, the mutual-exclusion law); the draws happen at the condensation (the recorded consumer, depth-7's road_musters) on each npc's own name stream — unborn until the reader's zone warms, canon after (first-commit-wins, never a redraw).

prohibitions.flaw: the scales tilt for old coin
prohibitions.notes: the market's floor under its own flaw (AP-8's prohibition surface, the first committed arming — the culture's limit over a member's flaw, what the lowlands CANNOT do; the WH40k grammar, prohibitions as pack metadata never bonuses, REFERENCES §10): however the weighbeam tilts toward old coin, a paying stranger of the road is never turned from the crossing's shelter — the trade's own law, older than the market's ledgers. Maren's flaw is the flaw this law bounds (the tilt stays legal against coin, illegal against shelter); the gate-review log assert reads it against the run.

lowland.notes: the river folk (the cultures slice, D-130: lowland traders vs hill folk): the crossing, the market, the levy and the manor — the bank's cast, plus the road traffic's lowland strangers. The custom vocabulary is the trade's own counting words (the river's name, the crossing's fee, the audit's paper, the market's beam and staff); the CK3 culture keying — one profile per culture, the members' generated_name declarations name it.

prohibitions.flaw: the iron hides when prices fall
prohibitions.notes: the crofts' limit under their own flaw (the second arming of AP-8's prohibition surface): the bloom may hide from the market's prices, but never from a blood price's payment — a wergeld once named stays named until it is paid, the feud's living memory walking the road (the carrier's goal carries the word). What the hills CANNOT do: let a named man-price lapse, however the iron hides. Garrick's flaw is the flaw this law bounds; the deep feud history (slice 3's cause tree) is the law's own backlog.

hill.notes: the croft folk: the smelt camps behind the keep, the estranged half of the valley — the smelter-master and the road traffic's hill carrier. The custom vocabulary is the camps' own words (the smelted iron, the fuel, the blood price the hills never un-name); the clipped hard profile keys the culture's names. Two prohibition sets, two vocabularies, two profiles — the estrangement-as-data family complete (the Disco Elysium shape: belief as rules the culture cannot cross).

entries.notes: the guild's flinch (the triangle's present-side arm): when the trade's posts hold fear past 30, the guild councils — the stalls bar, the heads come together. One spooked post reads fraction 50 (bar 20, 1-in-5 per beat); both posts read the full 40. The player tips it with the fire family — the alarm's spike and ripple are the levers, never a script gate.

the families' vigil (the triangle's deep-history arm): the grievance ratio over the two houses — threshold 50 means BOTH elders must cross the 40-bar before the vigil can fire (one woken house reads fraction 50, the deadband; both woken read bar 60). The wergeld wakes slowly and together, by design.

the watch's round (the triangle's escalation arm): the same fear axis as the guild, read at the trained bar — the merchants council at 30, the watch patrols at 40 (the bar the fear's own decay still leaves reachable a beat or two past the spike). The ladder between the two thresholds is the FNV cascade: rising danger moves the trade first, the crown's answer second.

factions.notes: the triangle (slice 3, D-130's FNV shape — depth-6's first committed arming): three ratio+threshold dynamics over the settlement cast's live axes; the player tips ratios through the ordinary verbs (the fire family's alarm spikes fear; the grief reaction wakes grievance), never script gates — the emergent many roads.
